lines.text: In the year ten twenty five, a Tamil fleet sailed out into the open sea.
Its target was Srivijaya, a sea power on the far side of the Bay of Bengal.
The Chola emperor Rajendra had sent it.
Chola ships first struck Palembang, the capital, its palace and its monasteries.
An inscription at Thanjavur says the Srivijayan king was taken prisoner.
It calls his land Kadaram, probably Kedah, on the Malay coast.
Why did the Cholas go? Historians disagree.
Some say prestige, the glory of a world conqueror. Others say protecting trade with China.
A Chinese writer says Srivijaya forced passing ships to stop at its ports.
But he wrote about two centuries later.
Most historians see fast raids and plunder, not lasting rule.
Still, Srivijaya's grip on the sea trade was weakened.
Our main evidence is one Chola inscription.
A thousand years ago, a Tamil fleet reached across the sea, and shook a sea power.
Follow Aazhi for the next chronicle.
